title: Apannaka Jataka - The Unreliable & Reliable
full_text:
In ancient times, in the ancient city of Benares, when King Brahmadatta ruled with righteousness, the Great Being (Bodhisattva) was born according to the ripening of his past meritorious deeds. In that life, he appeared as a noble exemplar of Sacca & Panna, demonstrating boundless wisdom and spotless compassion for all living beings.

At that time, a great trial arose in the realm. The king and his ministers, blinded by greed, transient pride, and false counsel, had strayed from the path of righteousness, imposing harsh taxes and causing distress among the people and the forest creatures. Seeing the distress of the realm, the Great Being stepped forward without fear for his own comfort or life.

Gathering the people and confronting the monarch in the royal courtyard, the Great Being spoke words of gentle yet unshakeable truth: "O King! A throne upheld by tyranny crumbles to dust, but a realm governed by virtue, justice, and loving-kindness flourishes like a banyan tree whose shade shelters travelers from every land. He who sows harm reaps sorrow, while he who guards the weak attains enduring peace."

Moved by the Great Being’s spotless purity and profound reasoning, the king renounced his unjust decrees, ordered granaries opened to feed the hungry, and declared total protection for all beasts and birds in the forest. The Great Being guided the realm in peace and virtue, teaching that moral integrity, selfless sacrifice, and steady wisdom are the highest ornaments of life, leading mortals safely across the ocean of worldly trials.
moral: Truth and steadfast wisdom guide travelers safely through treacherous mirages.

In ancient times, in the kingdom of Magadha, amid the bamboo groves of Rajagaha, the Great Being (Bodhisattva) was born according to the ripening of his past meritorious deeds. In that life, he appeared as a noble exemplar of Panna, demonstrating boundless wisdom and spotless compassion for all living beings.

At that time, a great trial arose in the realm. The king and his ministers, blinded by greed, transient pride, and false counsel, had strayed from the path of righteousness, imposing harsh taxes and causing distress among the people and the forest creatures. Seeing the distress of the realm, the Great Being stepped forward without fear for his own comfort or life.

Gathering the people and confronting the monarch in the royal courtyard, the Great Being spoke words of gentle yet unshakeable truth: "O King! A throne upheld by tyranny crumbles to dust, but a realm governed by virtue, justice, and loving-kindness flourishes like a banyan tree whose shade shelters travelers from every land. He who sows harm reaps sorrow, while he who guards the weak attains enduring peace."

Moved by the Great Being’s spotless purity and profound reasoning, the king renounced his unjust decrees, ordered granaries opened to feed the hungry, and declared total protection for all beasts and birds in the forest. The Great Being guided the realm in peace and virtue, teaching that moral integrity, selfless sacrifice, and steady wisdom are the highest ornaments of life, leading mortals safely across the ocean of worldly trials.
moral: Spirits rejoice in pure conduct and peaceful minds, not in the slaughter of innocent beasts.

In ancient times, in the royal capital of Mithila in the fertile realm of Videha, the Great Being (Bodhisattva) was born according to the ripening of his past meritorious deeds. In that life, he appeared as a noble exemplar of Samagga, demonstrating boundless wisdom and spotless compassion for all living beings.

At that time, a great trial arose in the realm. The king and his ministers, blinded by greed, transient pride, and false counsel, had strayed from the path of righteousness, imposing harsh taxes and causing distress among the people and the forest creatures. Seeing the distress of the realm, the Great Being stepped forward without fear for his own comfort or life.

Gathering the people and confronting the monarch in the royal courtyard, the Great Being spoke words of gentle yet unshakeable truth: "O King! A throne upheld by tyranny crumbles to dust, but a realm governed by virtue, justice, and loving-kindness flourishes like a banyan tree whose shade shelters travelers from every land. He who sows harm reaps sorrow, while he who guards the weak attains enduring peace."

Moved by the Great Being’s spotless purity and profound reasoning, the king renounced his unjust decrees, ordered granaries opened to feed the hungry, and declared total protection for all beasts and birds in the forest. The Great Being guided the realm in peace and virtue, teaching that moral integrity, selfless sacrifice, and steady wisdom are the highest ornaments of life, leading mortals safely across the ocean of worldly trials.
moral: United in harmony, the small lift the heavy net; divided by discord, they perish.

In that life, he appeared as a noble exemplar of Panna, demonstrating boundless wisdom and spotless compassion for all living beings.

At that time, a great trial arose in the realm. Moved by the Great Being’s spotless purity and profound reasoning, the king renounced his unjust decrees, ordered granaries opened to feed the hungry, and declared total protection for all beasts and birds in the forest.
